title: AWS CLI Using Wrong Account, Profile, or Region
symptom: AWS CLI commands execute against the wrong AWS account or region, creating resources in unintended locations.
initial_observations: Command executed without error, but resources do not appear in expected console.
Resource not found errors when querying existing resources.
environment: Developer or engineer workstation with multiple AWS profiles.

possible_causes.cause: Environment variable (AWS_PROFILE or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION) overriding credentials file
possible_causes.evidence_needed: aws configure list shows TYPE: env overriding config file.
possible_causes.remediation: Clear environment variables (`unset AWS_PROFILE AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`) or set intentionally.

investigation_steps.title: Check Active Configuration Precedence
investigation_steps.explanation: Display which configuration source is determining profile, region, and credentials.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Look at TYPE column (env, shared-credentials-file, config-file).

investigation_steps.title: Verify Authenticated IAM Caller Identity
investigation_steps.explanation: Print Account ID, UserId, and Arn of current credentials.

verification: aws sts get-caller-identity displays correct 12-digit Account ID.
prevention: Use prompt tools like `aws-vault` or `starship` to visibly display current AWS profile in shell prompt.
